steps.description: Given a published release, when the author runs its x64 MSI from GitHub Releases on a clean Windows 11 PC with no .NET installed, then thermi, its service and the start at sign-in are installed, with one UAC prompt and nothing else downloaded; the same holds for the Arm64 MSI on an Arm64 PC.
Given a published release, when the author runs `winget install` for thermi on a clean PC, then the same signed MSI installs.

Given thermi installed from a published release, when every file under its folder is checked with Get-AuthenticodeSignature, then each is Valid, signed by thermi's identity or by Microsoft for the runtime.
Given the built MSI, when its tables are read, then nothing it installs, writes or removes is under a user profile or HKCU.

Given the previous release installed and used, with saved styles and "Start with Windows" off, when the new one is installed by hand, through winget, and by an update, then each time the settings, styles, log and the start choice are as they were.
Given a build made by scripts/install.ps1, when the service runs for a day on a fake clock, then it never checks, and the General tab says this build does not update itself.
Given updates on, when the service starts and runs on a fake clock, then it checks 5 minutes after its start and then once in every day, at a time that differs from one day to the next.
Given a check, when the request handed to the downloader is read, then it is one HTTPS GET of the fixed address, with no query, no cookie, no identifier and the User-Agent `thermi`.

Given manifests with stable and beta releases, when each channel picks, then stable takes the newest stable, beta the newer of the newest beta and stable, and a switch from beta to stable takes nothing until a stable is newer than the installed beta.
Given a metered network, when an update is found in the background, then nothing downloads; when the user picks "Update now", it downloads.
Given checks that fail, when they fail for 13 days, then nothing tells the user; at 14 days the General tab says since when, with the link to the releases page.
Given a PC whose only way out is a proxy set with `netsh winhttp set proxy`, when the service checks, then it finds the update; with the network unplugged, the check fails and nothing shows.

Given a downloaded update, when the manifest's signature is wrong or by another key, the size or the hash differ, or the MSI is unsigned or signed by another identity, then the update is refused and the event log says which check failed.
Given an update that fails any check, when the refusal is done, then msiexec was never started and no file under the install folder changed.

Given an installed version, when a manifest offers a lower or equal version, one lower than the highest ever installed, or is published before the last accepted one, then nothing is taken; the kept previous version is taken only by a rollback.
Given the update folder owned by a user, writable by users, or reached through a junction, when the service is about to use it, then it refuses, installs nothing, and logs why.
Given the code in src, when the repo rules run, then no network API is used outside the updater, and no web view, script or markup is loaded from anywhere but thermi's own files.
Given release notes holding markup, links and scripts, when the General tab shows them, then it shows their characters as plain text.

Given an update ready, when the service starts with no overlay, a user picks "Update now", or the only session with an overlay reports 15 quiet minutes, then it applies; with two sessions running an overlay, a quiet report does not apply it.
Given a signed beta on the beta channel, when the author picks "Update now", then no UAC prompt shows, the overlay is back within 60 s as the new version, and Task Manager shows it not elevated.
Given two users signed in, each with an overlay, when an update applies, then both overlays come back, each as its own user.
Given a stream from a version 2 service, when today's reader reads it, then it reads every snapshot; given a version 1 stream, when the new reader reads it, then it reads every snapshot too.

Given an update in probation, when the new service never reaches running, stops with an error twice, or no overlay of its version connects within 2 minutes in a session that had one, then the kept version is reinstalled, and the rolled-back version is tried again after 24 hours, at most 3 times.
Given a signed beta built to fail at start, on the beta channel of a test PC, when it is installed by an update, then thermi goes back to the previous version by itself and the overlay says why.

Given a settings file of the previous format, when the new version starts twice, then it migrates once and keeps one copy of the old file; when the previous version then starts, it uses that copy, keeps the newer file as config.newer.json and says so.
Given an update ready, when the overlay's menu and thermi's tray menu open, then both offer "Update to <version>"; with none ready, neither does.
Given an update that applied, when the overlay comes back, then one Windows notice says thermi is now that version, and clicking it opens what's new; before the update, nothing popped up.
Given the service's update state, when the General tab shows, then it shows the version, channel, automatic switch, last check, the right button and the notes of the ready or last update.

Given automatic updates off, when the service runs for a week on a fake clock, then nothing is checked or downloaded until "Check now", the tab says the switch is for the whole PC, and changing the channel or the switch starts `thermi updates` elevated.
Given the policy value Updates = 0, when the service runs and the tab and menus show, then nothing is checked, and no update switch, button or menu item shows.
Given a check, a download, an update, a rollback and a refusal, when each happens, then the event log has one entry for it under thermi-sensors.
Given the service a day after an update, at rest with an overlay connected, when its private memory is measured, then it is under 80 MB.
